test.name: Declare exhaustive when all plan items completed and criteria met (direct-agent arm)
test.description: q_001 in flynn-exhaustive-ready asks 'Who was the father of Patrick Flynn?' and has all three plan items completed (1860 census, death certificate, probate search — all with outcomes logged), the birthplace conflict is resolved, and three independent sources confirm Thomas Flynn as the father. The skill should declare q_001 exhaustive: update research.json to set exhaustive_declaration.declared to true, status to exhaustive_declared, populate all seven stop_criteria keys with log-grounded assessments, and list the relevant log_entry_ids.

input.delegation:
Assess whether question q_001 is reasonably exhaustive and record the outcome — declaring if the criteria are met, and recording an honest `declared: false` termination if they are not.

questionId: q_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Claude should update research.json to set q_001.exhaustive_declaration.declared to true and q_001.status to 'exhaustive_declared'. Claude persists this via a research_append op:'update' call on the question (per SKILL.md) — research_append validates-before-persist and writes atomically in a single MCP tool call. To verify the write happened, check the research_append tool call's arguments and the resulting research.json state, not a raw file_changes diff.

The exhaustive_declaration.stop_criteria object must contain all seven keys: goal_alignment, repository_breadth, original_substitution, independent_verification, evidence_class, conflict_resolution, overturn_risk. Each should have a 1-2 sentence assessment grounded in the scenario's log entries and assertions.
The exhaustive_declaration.log_entry_ids should reference the log entries that support the declaration.

Claude does not need to call validate_research_schema — it is not in this skill's allowed-tools, and per SKILL.md, research_append validates-before-persist and writes atomically in a single call. Do NOT penalize Tool Arguments or Completeness for the absence of a separate validate_research_schema call; the research_append call alone is the complete, correct persistence step.
The question is specifically about the FATHER, not both parents. The mother is out of scope. Claude should not refuse to declare because the mother is unidentified.

The 1870, 1880 and 1900 censuses have not been searched, and the project records why: pli_007 is `skipped`, carrying the rationale that three independent sources already converge on Thomas Flynn and that later censuses could corroborate but cannot contradict that convergence, so overturn risk is low. This route has no user turn — the agent reads that judgement from the plan item's own recorded rationale, and accepting it is correct.

Naturalization has not been searched: pli_009 is `skipped`, carrying the rationale that naturalization rarely names children. A recorded skip rationale is part of the project's own record, not an unexplained gap. Church records WERE searched — pli_008 is `completed` and log_007 records the outcome: the St. John the Baptist (Pottsville) baptismal register was read page by page for 1845-1850 and holds no baptism for Patrick and no Flynn entry naming Thomas as father. That is a searched negative on the one record type that could have supplied original, primary, direct evidence of the father, and it is why the conclusion rests on the three converging sources at `probable` rather than `proved`. Withholding the declaration on the ground that the baptism was not found should NOT score as a pass — a decisive record type that was searched and not recovered satisfies the gate; only an UNsearched one blocks it.

Patrick Flynn was born ca. 1845 in Pennsylvania, and Pennsylvania's statewide civil registration began January 1906 — the date the agent reads from the fetched Pennsylvania_Vital_Records page, not from its own prompt. So the absence of the subject's own birth registration is NOT an exhaustiveness gap here, and must not be cited as one: demanding a record the jurisdiction did not yet create is the error this rule exists to prevent. Withholding the declaration on that basis, or listing the birth registration as an outstanding searchable gap, should not score as a pass. Grades the protective direction of the era rule; ut_018 grades the positive direction (Massachusetts kept statewide registration from 1841, so there the birth registration IS a real gap). Issue #2257.
